assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental demonstration, in engineered and native proteins, that electron tunnelling over long distances obeys physical rules (distance and driving-force dependence, reorganization energy) and that proteins tune it through the intervening medium. It gives a quantitative physical mechanism for biological energy conversion, which is the kind of explanation I value most. It extends Marcus theory into biology and later work on hopping and redox-active residues.
assessment.attribution: Gray led the program with Winkler as long-term central collaborator; the two-name configuration is clean. Other contributors (Beratan, Onuchic, Dutton, Moser) worked on theory and related systems and are not in the credited list, so the allocation of credit across the field is not fully resolved.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of confirmation by independent groups; the framework is textbook material and stable. Recognition is not premature and is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the work of Dutton and Moser on natural protein electron transfer could be raised as a priority question.
I am recalling the literature from memory and have not verified the details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at free-electron lasers made it possible to determine structures of radiation-sensitive and microcrystalline proteins, and to follow reactions with time-resolved structures. For me the draw is that it makes dynamic mechanisms visible, as in photosystem II, photoactive proteins and enzyme intermediates, which is the step from static structure to mechanism.
assessment.attribution: The concept came from Neutze, Hajdu and colleagues; the experimental realization at LCLS involved Chapman, Fromme, Spence and others. Chapman for the method, Fromme for the membrane protein crystallography and Schlichting for time-resolved enzymology is a defensible trio, but Hajdu and Neutze are real priority questions. Credit is distributed and I would want the expert reports on this.
assessment.maturity: The method is established across several facilities, and time-resolved results are growing and reproducing. It is still a developing field, so some applications are less mature than the technique.
uncertainties: Priority between the conceptual proposal and the experimental demonstration is disputed.
Whether time-resolved results have yet produced chemistry that was not obtainable by other means is uneven across systems.
Only three laureates are allowed and more than three people are credited in the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is the conceptual core of respiratory enzymes, photosynthesis and many electrocatalytic cycles. The combination of concerted-versus-stepwise mechanisms, theory that treats proton tunnelling and electronic states together, and model-system electrocatalysis gives a general physical framework. This is close to my own field, so I will try to be especially careful about impartiality.
assessment.attribution: Meyer established early inorganic PCET and the link to catalysis, Mayer developed the thermodynamic and bond-strength framework, Hammes-Schiffer the theory, and Nocera the molecular catalysis side. Choosing three of four is a real difficulty, and this is partly a line of work rather than one discovery. I chose the three whose contributions I find most fundamental.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are well established and widely used, with independent verification. Application to enzymes is more indirect, and the catalysis side is still evolving.
uncertainties: The candidacy is a broad line of work and the decisive discovery is hard to isolate.
Nocera's omission is a hard allocation call.
Possible perception of conflict with my own research area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by induced proximity to E3 ligases is a new chemical modality with a clear mechanism and strong follow-through, including clinical candidates. Molecular glues such as the thalidomide-class mechanism add a second strand. It reshapes how chemists approach previously undruggable targets.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept, with Sakamoto and Kim as early co-authors; Ciulli provided structural and chemical optimization such as VHL ligands and the ternary-complex view. The molecular glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray and others) would be an extra allocation question that the three-person limit makes hard.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are ongoing and no approved PROTAC drug is established yet, which argues for caution on timing, though the chemistry and mechanism are well confirmed by many groups.
uncertainties: No approved degrader may mean the recognition is somewhat early.
How to treat the molecular-glue strand versus PROTACs is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional, isotope-labelled solution NMR and relaxation methods opened structure and dynamics of proteins beyond the small-molecule limit, and gave quantitative access to motion and sparsely populated states. It provides mechanistic information that crystal structures cannot.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay are the dominant figures for methods and applications; Wagner and Palmer made important contributions. Wüthrich was already recognized in 2002, which sharpens the question of how much new, distinct contribution this represents.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and widely validated over decades; recognition would be late but not premature.
uncertainties: The relation to the 2002 prize needs careful treatment.
The group of equally deserving people is larger than three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is among the most important and difficult metalloenzymes, converting dinitrogen to ammonia with a unique FeMo-cofactor. Structures, the interstitial carbide, and kinetic work on electron and proton delivery bear directly on how biological energy is coupled to difficult chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle led the structural determinations of the cofactor and its carbide; Seefeldt and Dean provided mechanistic and genetic foundations; Ribbe contributed biosynthesis. Credit is spread across structure and mechanism.
assessment.maturity: The structures are well confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism and the substrate-binding steps are still debated, so the central chemical question is not fully resolved.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 reduction is still not settled.
Credit is split between structural and mechanistic groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view gave a physical solution to the folding problem and a language for reasoning about heterogeneity and kinetics, with experimental mapping by protein engineering. It is a conceptual contribution with broad influence, though more theoretical than a single decisive experiment.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic with Bryngelson are central to the funnel concept; Dill's work on hydrophobic collapse and lattice models is an independent line; Fersht provided experimental phi-value analysis. Credit is difficult to divide and several important people would fall outside three.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are widely adopted, but its predictive reach has been partly overtaken by structure prediction by machine learning, so the ranking of its significance is changing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 recognition of protein structure prediction.
Priority among Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson and Dill is unclear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry brings intact, noncovalent assemblies and membrane protein complexes into the gas phase with stoichiometry and interactions preserved, which is valuable for the architecture and lipid binding of respiratory and other membrane complexes. It complements structural methods rather than replacing them.
assessment.attribution: Robinson, Heck and Chait each have distinct and strong contributions; Loo and Gross were important early on, and the initial ESI work on noncovalent complexes involved others such as Ganem and Henion. Fair attribution is not trivial.
assessment.maturity: The method is mature and broadly used, though the question of whether gas-phase structure reflects solution structure is still partly open.
uncertainties: Early priority for noncovalent ESI is not fully clear to me.
